omissions.interpretation: Grouped using kernel names and scoped adapter semantics; summed isolated kernel medians are missing-work estimates, not additive latency corrections. FP32 GEMM API attribution remains inferred from FEMU stubs unless independently traced.

native_kernel_calibration.scope: Original generate_custom_voice, including text tokenization, autoregressive talker and code predictor, speech decoder and CPU waveform return; no file encoding. BF16 resident parameters and FA2.

limitations: GX replays the scalar control tape of one calibrated real request. Original GPU scalar read operations remain except those explicitly removed by the optimization. This is not a predictor of numerical outputs, new prompts or arbitrary generated lengths.

GX-only known-unique token-suppression and empty-padding adapters omit native uniqueness/nonzero work; native validation uses the original operations. Baseline omissions are quantified separately; sums of isolated kernel durations are not end-to-end corrections.

Native calibration includes 1378 FP32 GEMM launches absent from GX timing (11.205365ms summed isolated medians), plus cuDNN plan/grid discrepancies. The integer-position candidate introduces 117 additional uncovered operation launches in mode2; exact coverage and misses are stored per run. Missing predictions are not measured zero-cost work.

Mode3 uses10us epochs. Numerous tiny operations make epoch granularity relevant; mode3 absolute latency is not demonstrated to be a more accurate hardware estimate. Both predictions substantially exceed the native request time.

CPU instruction calibration has 2822 unresolved out of63818 samples (4.42%); GX host EPYC7702P differs from native A100 host EPYC9554. Simulation uses one measured request per variant/mode, after a warmup.

GX and matched native control validation include Python control-tape hooks. The primary native latency validation uses the public API without those hooks; its absolute timing is therefore not a matched-instrumentation calibration of GX.

The uninstrumented native first baseline warmup had a different hash; all20 measured outputs and the other7 warmups match. The differing cold baseline output was finite with the same length and extrema, but waveform error was not retained. Control-checked native all28 outputs match. No all-cold-start determinism claim.

Integer positions are validated for binary attention masks and supported context lengths. Float/nonfinite inputs to the generic packed check retain the original path. Numerical native checks cover one prompt, seed, shape and single GPU, not all generation modes or concurrent requests.
Compact traces contain per-bin unions of CPU/GPU/copy intervals; overlapping categories are not additive hardware utilization. Full archived traces remain available by recorded paths.
